key_insight: CT-Navigator uses generalist multimodal AI to explore CT scans progressively and invoke radiology tools, grounding answers in traceable visual evidence.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more transparent CT interpretation, but the abstract does not establish safety or effectiveness in clinical practice.
method: Navigate from whole scans to individual slices and regions of interest.
Train with 8,904 visual chain-of-thought trajectories for agentic supervised fine-tuning.
Apply reinforcement learning on 33,219 questions, prioritizing informative training signals.
evidence_signal: CT-Navigator achieved 79.50% accuracy on the new 7,000-question CTNavi-Bench, with a reported 17.59% gain over the strongest baseline and strong generalization across three external CT benchmarks.
watch_item: Benchmark performance and traceable visual evidence do not establish clinical reliability; prospective workflow validation remains necessary.
paper_title: CT-Navigator: Towards Interpretable and Generalizable CT Understanding through Agentic Perception and Tool-Invocation
